label: <DEL> step of short sequences (L<=4), token-dependent
explanation: Reset-gate neuron that fires almost only on the <DEL> delimiter step (89% of activation mass), and strongly favours short sequences: about 82% of <DEL> steps fire at L=3, 40% at L=4, 14% at L=5, and almost none at L>=6. Among short sequences, the original-token content modulates both whether it fires and how strongly. Sequences starting with g, 3, r, l or i fire most, and the top activations are g e j <DEL>, g h j <DEL>, r j k <DEL>. A secondary component (about 11% of mass, weaker) fires when the letter v is input at original positions 2-4 (in_first). It never fires in the copy phase, at t=0 or t=1, or on repeated tokens. The predicate misses the v activations and the L=5 <DEL> activations, and it over-predicts L=4 <DEL> steps whose content does not favour it (dev F1 0.53, mass recall 0.73; adding the v clause raises mass recall to 0.83).
